intent: Change one thing: move all five sensors forward from y = 0.04 m to y = 0.06 m, keeping spread, size, wheels, body and mass as before. I expect fewer off-track ends and more progress on the development tracks, because the controller will see the line earlier and max_error should fall below the 0.06 m limit. I am considering, but not committing to, a wider spread (x = ±0.032 m) if line losses rise on the sharpest bend after this change. I am also considering a smaller mass if oscillation stays high.
learning: Hypotheses for this race: (1) moving the sensors to y = 0.06 m reduces max_error below 0.06 m and cuts off-track ends, which tests the late-reaction explanation; (2) progress rises above 0.2 on all tracks; (3) line_loss_events stay at or below 2 per run, which would show the spread of ±0.024 m is still adequate. If max_error still reaches the limit with more look-ahead, the cause is more likely the controller gain or base speed than geometry, and I will say so in the next proposal.
rationale: The race evidence for the iteration-0 design is poor on all three development tracks. Every one of the 60 trials ended off track, with progress of only 0.105 (oval), 0.156 (s-bend) and 0.113 (slalom). Mean max_error sits at about 0.061 to 0.062 m, which is the 0.06 m off-track limit. So the robot is drifting out of the line early in each run, not slowly losing time. Line losses are low (1 per run on oval and s-bend, 2 on slalom), so the sensors are still seeing the tape most of the time. The Integrator's rule applies: high max_error with few line losses points to late reaction, so I adopt their advice and move all sensors forward from y = 0.04 m to y = 0.06 m. That gives the controller about 60 mm of look-ahead, up from 40 mm. I am keeping the sensor spread at ±0.024 m, because line_loss_events do not point to a narrow spread. I am also keeping the body and drivetrain unchanged, to isolate the forward-offset effect. Body width cannot widen the off-track limit: max(0.06, 0.0125 + body_width/4) stays at 0.06 for any allowed body width, so it is not a lever. I expect fewer off-track ends and longer progress, with max_error falling below 0.06 on the s-bend and slalom. The main risk is that the look-ahead overshoots on the tighter bends.
